```{r library}
library(quorum)
```

## Why

Study A0 resolved 200 site-by-season nitrogen decisions by hand, walking a
two-lens cascade cell by cell: a mechanism lens built from a PESTO ensemble,
and a statistical lens built from the hub's mixed model. The question an
analyst closing out that study asks is a package question, not a study
question: *if I hand quorum exactly what each lens contributed at each of
those 200 cells, does the package's general-purpose resolution reproduce the
cascade the study hand-wrote -- tier by tier, lens by lens, rate by rate --
and what would have happened at the handful of cells where the cascade itself
gave up?* This vignette answers both halves on the fixture the study
recorded, with no simulator run and no network call.

## What

Three verbs carry the whole of this vignette. `lens_contribution()` builds
one row of what a single lens contributed to one decision cell: whether its
estimate is grounded, whether it abstained, the action it stands behind, and
the reason and grounding token it declared. `contributions()` row-binds
those parts into the table a resolution reads. `quorum_resolve()` walks a
`quorum_policy()`'s declared fallback order over that table and returns,
cell by cell, which lens's answer is carried, whether the cell decided,
defaulted to the status quo, or abstained, and the action that follows.
`quorum_compare_policies()` runs several policies over the same
contributions table at once, so the cost of a fallback convention is a column
rather than an argument.

## Do

### The fixture

The 200 recorded cells ship with the package as `a0_cells.rds`. The lookup
below reaches the installed copy through `system.file()` and falls back to
the path relative to this vignette's own source directory, so the same code
renders whether the package is installed or only loaded from its source tree.

```{r read-fixture}
a0_path <- system.file("extdata", "a0_cells.rds", package = "quorum")
if (!nzchar(a0_path)) {
  a0_path <- "../inst/extdata/a0_cells.rds"
}
tab_a0 <- readRDS(a0_path)
nrow(tab_a0)
```

```{r fixture-facts, echo = FALSE}
facts <- data.frame(
  fact = c(
    "decision cells", "status-quo rate (kg N/ha)",
    "safe (no-input) rate (kg N/ha)", "candidate rate grid (kg N/ha)",
    "source"
  ),
  value = c(
    as.character(nrow(tab_a0)),
    as.character(attr(tab_a0, "status_quo_rate")),
    as.character(attr(tab_a0, "safe_rate")),
    paste(attr(tab_a0, "rate_vec"), collapse = ", "),
    attr(tab_a0, "source")
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  facts, col.names = c("Fact", "Value"),
  caption = "What the shipped fixture carries."
)
```

Each row of `tab_a0` is one site-by-season cell, carrying what the mechanism
lens and the statistical lens each contributed to it -- their grounding,
whether they abstained, and their proposed rate -- together with the
cascade's own recorded tiers and rate, so the resolution below can be checked
against them without recomputing either lens.

### Building the contributions table

`.a0_contributions()` reads only the recorded *input* columns and builds one
`lens_contribution()` row per lens per cell, exactly as the package's own
characterisation test does; the recorded *output* columns (`tier_mechanism`,
`cascade_lens`, `verdict`, `action_rate`, ...) are read nowhere in this
function, because they are what the resolution is checked against, not what
it is built from.

```{r contributions}
a0_contributions <- function(tab) {
  cell <- paste0(tab$site_id, "_", tab$season)
  s1 <- nrow(tab)
  rows <- vector("list", 2L * s1)
  for (i1 in seq_len(s1)) {
    row_mech <- lens_contribution(
      "mechanism",
      grounded = tab$grounded[i1],
      abstained = tab$dec_abstained[i1],
      action = tab$dec_action[i1],
      reason = tab$dec_reason[i1],
      grounding = tab$dec_grounding[i1]
    )
    row_mech$cell <- cell[i1]
    row_mech$lenses_disagree <- tab$lenses_disagree[i1]
    row_mech$producer_abstained <- tab$producer_abstained[i1]
    rows[[i1]] <- row_mech
    row_stat <- lens_contribution(
      "statistical",
      grounded = tab$stat_available[i1],
      abstained = tab$stat_abstained[i1],
      action = tab$stat_action[i1],
      reason = tab$stat_reason[i1]
    )
    row_stat$cell <- cell[i1]
    rows[[s1 + i1]] <- row_stat
  } # ends i1, over the recorded decision cells
  contributions(rows)
}

contrib_a0 <- a0_contributions(tab_a0)
nrow(contrib_a0)
```

Four hundred rows: two lenses at each of the 200 cells.

### Resolving the cascade

The cascade is a `quorum_policy()` with two lenses in fallback order --
mechanism first, statistical second -- and the study's own status-quo rate as
the fallback for a cell where a grounded lens declined to decide.

```{r resolve}
policy_a0 <- quorum_policy(
  order = c("mechanism", "statistical"),
  status_quo = attr(tab_a0, "status_quo_rate")
)
res_a0 <- quorum_resolve(contrib_a0, policy_a0)
head(res_a0[, c("cell", "carried_lens", "verdict", "action")])
```

```{r crosstab}
cross_tab <- table(res_a0$carried_lens)
matches_recorded <- identical(res_a0$carried_lens, tab_a0$cascade_lens) &&
  identical(res_a0$verdict, tab_a0$verdict) &&
  identical(res_a0$action, tab_a0$action_rate)
```

```{r crosstab-kable, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(cross_tab, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  col.names = c("Carried lens", "Cells"),
  caption = paste0(
    "Cells resolved by carried lens (n = ", sum(cross_tab), ")."
  )
)
```

### The cost of the two committed conventions

Study A0's cascade is not the only way to resolve an abstention. Two earlier
conventions are kept as first-class `policy_committed()` objects: one
resolves an abstention to the safe (no-input) rate, one resolves it to the
status quo. `quorum_compare_policies()` prices all three on the same
contributions table.

```{r compare-policies}
sq_rate <- attr(tab_a0, "status_quo_rate")
safe_rate <- attr(tab_a0, "safe_rate")
cmp_a0 <- quorum_compare_policies(contrib_a0, list(
  cascade = policy_a0,
  prior_zero = policy_committed(
    "zero", lens = "mechanism", status_quo = sq_rate, safe_action = safe_rate
  ),
  prior_status_quo = policy_committed(
    "status_quo", lens = "mechanism", status_quo = sq_rate,
    safe_action = safe_rate
  )
))
verdict_counts <- data.frame(
  policy = c("cascade", "fixed to safe rate", "fixed to status quo"),
  decide = c(
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_cascade == "decide"),
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_prior_zero == "decide"),
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_prior_status_quo == "decide")
  ),
  default = c(
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_cascade == "default"),
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_prior_zero == "default"),
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_prior_status_quo == "default")
  ),
  abstain = c(
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_cascade == "abstain"),
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_prior_zero == "abstain"),
    sum(cmp_a0$verdict_prior_status_quo == "abstain")
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r compare-policies-kable, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  verdict_counts,
  caption = paste0(
    "How each policy resolves the same ", nrow(cmp_a0), " cells."
  )
)
```

### A figure: the constraint that moves the cascade

Every recorded cell also carries `constrained`, Study A0's flag for whether the
mechanism model's response at that site-season hides a constraint the field
data alone would not reveal. The figure below reads carried lens against that
flag directly from `res_a0` and `tab_a0$constrained`; it shows something the
tables above do not, because neither cross-tab conditions on the flag.

```{r fig-cascade-by-constraint, echo = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), fig.cap = "Carried lens by decision cell, split by whether Study A0 recorded a hidden constraint at that site-season. Constrained cells fall back to the statistical lens far more often than unconstrained ones."}
plot_df <- data.frame(
  constrained = ifelse(tab_a0$constrained, "constrained", "unconstrained"),
  carried_lens = res_a0$carried_lens,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ggplot2::ggplot(
  plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = constrained, fill = carried_lens)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar(position = "stack") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "carried lens") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "recorded constraint flag", y = "decision cells",
    title = "Which lens the cascade carries, by recorded constraint"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

```{r fig-cascade-skip, echo = FALSE, eval = !requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), results = "asis"}
cat("ggplot2 is not installed; the constraint-split figure is skipped.\n")
```

## Read

The resolution reproduces the recorded cascade exactly:
`r if (matches_recorded) "every column checked above (carried lens, verdict, action) is identical to the recorded table, cell for cell." else "at least one column diverges from the recorded table (see the assertion above)."`
Of the `r sum(cross_tab)` cells, the mechanism lens carries
`r unname(cross_tab["mechanism"])`, the statistical lens carries
`r unname(cross_tab["statistical"])`, and `r unname(cross_tab["status quo"])`
default to the status quo because a grounded lens was present but would not
stand behind a number. No cell abstains in this fixture: a grounded lens
covers every cell, if only after falling back to the status quo.

The committed-convention table shows what changes under the two fallback
conventions the cascade replaced. Both fixed conventions decide (or default)
every cell they touch and never abstain, because a fixed convention mints a
rate for whatever the mechanism lens contributed, grounded or not. The
cascade is the only policy of the three under which a cell can carry no
number at all -- though on this particular fixture, as the table shows, it
never needs to. The figure makes the mechanism behind the split visible:
a constrained site-season is far more likely to fall through to the
statistical lens, because the mechanism model's plateau is exactly what a
constraint distorts.

## Limits

This fixture is Study A0's synthetic belt, not a field trial: the recorded
grounding, abstention and action columns are a study's committed inputs, not
a re-derivation of the mechanism or statistical lens from raw data, so this
vignette shows resolution mechanics, not model fitting. The loss figures
attached to Study A0 -- the cascade returning a summed loss over the belt of 2,960 AUD per hectare against 5,818 AUD per hectare for a naive always-mechanism rule -- come
from the study's own economic ledger and are not recomputed here; they are
cited, not reproduced, and a reader who needs them should follow the pointer
to the study's own report rather than trust an inline number this vignette
never computes. Agreement between the two lenses at a cell is not established
or exercised here either: this vignette reads recorded per-lens contributions,
not independent posterior draws, so `quorum_independence()` and
`agreement_pairwise()` play no part in it -- see *Adding a lens* for both.

## What to read next

*Adding a lens* builds the lens contract from the ground up and works through
a TMB adapter, including the agreement and independence machinery this
vignette does not exercise. *Getting started with quorum* walks the three
on-ramps -- ensemble ingestion, surrogate emulation, and the koine fourth
opinion -- that turn a non-hub estimate into a lens in the first place.
*Distribution-preserving surrogates* is the full worked loop behind the
mechanism lens's ensemble: ingest, emulate, invert, and check.

## Reproduce

This vignette draws no random numbers: every result is a deterministic
function of the shipped fixture and the package's own resolution code.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
